companies.name: Dawn
companies.description: Dawn is building VIM (Virtual Intelligent Mentor), a lightweight AR glasses paired with intelligent software designed for frontline manufacturing workers. VIM combines AI with traditional shop-floor resources to deliver workers instant and hands-free access to the knowledge they need. By closing the skill gap, reducing downtime, and modernizing training, Dawn helps manufacturers boost productivity and preserve expertise.

companies.name: ReGlove
companies.description: ReGlove is building an AI-powered rehabilitation glove designed to help stroke survivors regain motor control and independence in their daily lives. By supporting natural grasping motions, ReGlove empowers patients to perform everyday activities—like holding a cup of coffee or buttoning a shirt—while also serving as a tool for continuous rehabilitation beyond the clinic. Their mission is to make recovery more accessible, effective, and motivating for millions of people living with the long-term effects of stroke.

companies.name: Ludus
companies.description: Ludus eliminates manual flashcard creation for language students. Open any word in our pre-loaded dictionaries, click save, and it’s automatically added to your personalized study deck.

companies.name: Hearify
companies.description: Hearify is an application that eases the process of aural rehabilitation for members of the hard-of-hearing community, saving countless hours of audiologist training by allowing one to practice from the comfort of their own home. Built with features to mimic all aspects of auditory training, from matched pair sets to sound and word recognition, the app also implements AI analytics and features to complement the work of an audiologist. This application saves time and revolutionizes the process of aural rehabilitation present today.

companies.name: Wagoo
companies.description: Wagoo is developing a voice-first productivity assistant that answers questions and completes tasks. All with just a push of a button, with hundreds of integrations. Schedule meetings, respond to emails, search the web, plan your day, have conversations, and so much more.

companies.name: Vitband
companies.description: Vitband is the first wearable device that tracks muscles in real time. Powered by our patent-pending sEMG technology, it helps athletes optimize training load and find personalized sweet spots for peak performance. By tracking muscle strength, activation, and fatigue in real time, it tells athletes exactly when to push, when to recover, and how to avoid injury. Backed by UC Berkeley and Stanford University, and trusted by Olympians, Vitband transforms raw muscle signals into actionable insights for athletes to reach their full potential.

companies.name: PollenPal
companies.description: PollenPal is an AI-powered monitoring system designed for beekeepers, using beehive-mounted devices with computer vision and sensors to detect threats like varroa mites and invasive bee species. Built for easy deployment, it delivers real-time alerts and offers actionable insights, helping operations save on replacement costs while improving margins through efficient management. With solutions for both hobbyists and large farms, PollenPal bridges tech gaps in an aging industry facing billions in annual losses.

companies.name: Manglovo Health
companies.description: Manglovo Health is a biotech startup advancing next-generation therapeutics and technologies in reproductive health. Our lead asset is a uterine-selective estrogen receptor antagonist, being developed as a once-weekly oral contraceptive without hormones.

companies.name: Created by
companies.description: Created by chefs for chefs, ROA is an AI-powered SaaS platform that revolutionizes restaurant operations by addressing food waste, high labor turnover, and narrow margins. Our kitchen-native solution—combining semantic recipe management, invoice-based inventory tracking, and POS-aware demand forecasting—empowers chefs to streamline kitchen workflows and optimise resource allocation.

companies.name: Silo
companies.description: Silo is an automated portfolio generator tailored for engineers. Users upload their work artifacts—such as code repositories, PDFs, and CAD diagrams—and Silo's in-house LLM pipeline creates a professional portfolio hosted on a customizable URL.

companies.name: Saturn
companies.description: Saturn is like a mutual fund for the blockchain being built on Solana. By minting Saturn tokens, which each represent an actively managed portfolio through fundamental and eventually quantitative management, we unify the best of the blockchain ecosystem into a single token, giving users diversified exposure to digital asset innovation. Unlike traditional funds, on-chain investments offer full transparency, instant liquidity, and access to high-growth sectors like DeFi and Web3. Saturn provides a seamless way for everyone to participate in cutting-edge blockchain projects, making investing in crypto simpler, more efficient, and potentially more rewarding.

companies.name: SWERV

companies.name: Sante Health
companies.description: Sante Health is a startup leveraging AI to help governments, health insurers, and hospitals manage infectious disease outbreaks. Our machine learning model uses epidemiological, climate, and urban spatial data to identify high-risk areas and predict outbreaks before they happen, enabling proactive health interventions to protect communities. We have already developed our first MVP for dengue prediction in Brazil and are now advancing scalable, data-driven solutions to improve healthcare resource allocation.

In fluid mechanics, chaotic and disorderly flow (i.e., turbulent flow) leads to increased mixing, high pressure drops, and significant energy losses. Because of its chaotic nature, accurately predicting and controlling turbulent flow has been a long-standing engineering challenge plaguing nearly every major industry. This forces design engineers to rely on approximations, extensive physical prototyping, and costly trial-and-error iterations. ReynKo’s breakthrough mathematical framework is the first of its kind, and bridges the gap in our understanding of turbulent flow, enabling an entirely new class of highly efficient and accurate fluid simulations. These tools allow for predictive engineering that takes place virtually, eliminating the need for physical prototyping and saving significant amounts of time and money.

companies.name: REPS
companies.description: Turning roads into powerplants. REPS is turning roads into powerplants, by efficiently generating green electricity from lost energy in traffic. Their first live "Road Energy Production System" went operational in November 2025, and has already been validated by 85,000+ heavy trucks under real-world conditions. They’re starting with roads (~$400bn annual electricity market), and then unlocking the $1T+ global energy-harvesting opportunity. ‍ About the Tech There are two well-known solution approaches in the field of energy harvesting: piezoelectric effects and dynamo principles. Piezoelectric systems fail due to a simple physical limitation. The deformation of the crystals that induces voltage occurs only within the micrometer range. Energy yield is always linearly dependent on displacement, regardless of the efficiency or durability of the energy converter. Ultimately, the limitation is rooted in a fundamental physical principle. Dynamo principles, on the other hand, require translational motion to be converted into rotational motion. Mechanical friction components wear out, especially under the high frequencies and masses encountered in road traffic environments. Furthermore, in order to fully convert the impulse of a vehicle, a dynamo must either: a) Spin for approximately two minutes. In that case, when the next impulse arrives after, for example, ten seconds, it cannot efficiently convert additional energy because it is still processing the previous impulse. b) Use multiple dynamos, which quickly becomes economically unattractive. c) Be configured for stronger resistance, resulting in shorter spin times, but creating an extremely inefficient performance range across varying vehicle masses. d) Combine multiple approaches, which again becomes economically unviable. e) and so on Our best energy converters, developed through more than 100 years of research, fail in terms of efficiency and durability once they are removed from application fields where constant forces are acting and placed into environments characterized by irregular, high-magnitude impulses occurring at unpredictable intervals. They have developed a mechanism based on the world’s first permanent magnetic bearing. In combination with electromagnetic induction, this means the system operates with virtually no mechanical friction and therefore does not suffer from conventional wear. At the same time, impulses ranging from 1 to 40 tons within 0.07 seconds can be converted with high efficiency. This does not only mean that a profitable business model becomes possible. It means that they have unlocked the key to the field of energy harvesting, with the potential to radically and positively transform both the energy crisis and the climate crisis. About the Team Their team built the worldwide first running road power plant. companies.name: Gentian
companies.description: Nature underpins economies and public services—from productive land and forests to water, flood protection and resilient cities. Yet businesses and governments increasingly need to understand what nature they depend on, how it is changing, and what risks that creates. Over half of the world's GDP depends on this. The problem is that the data needed to answer these questions is often slow, expensive and difficult to obtain. At Gentian, we solve this data problem. Traditional ecological surveys are largely manual, making it difficult and expensive to establish biodiversity baselines, identify nature-related risks, monitor change, or meet regulations such as TNFD and Biodiversity Net Gain. Gentian combines AI with very high-resolution satellite and hyperspectral imagery to automate this work. We can map habitats, individual trees, peatlands, invasive species and other ecological features across very large areas in days - or, in some cases, minutes - turning months of fieldwork into actionable, regulation-ready data. This enables infrastructure, energy, forestry, mining and public-sector organisations to reduce survey costs and delays, identify nature risks earlier, and make better decisions about land. companies.name: Aspect Aerospace
companies.description: At Aspect Aerospace, we are announcing a new piece of revolutionary tech for the space industry. We are leveraging our TRL-9 hardware and software to create a "Single-Board Satellite" -- the entire satellite is a single printed circuit board, able to be mass produced in any PCB assembly house in the US. Each satellite will be 10cm x 10cm to fit inside a CubeSat-sized deployer, with the option to be larger for specialized scenarios. Our goal is to leverage this breakthrough tech to create a space industry in Mobile, Alabama. Leveraging the single-board satellite architecture, we're bringing to market a "constellation in-a-box" -- a whole constellation of 20-100 satellites, deployed from a single CubeSat, for less than the cost of a single CubeSat. Each satellite would cost hundreds of dollars, rather than traditional hundreds of thousands or millions of dollars. With each satellite acting as a node in a constellation, we can do some revolutionary things, each constellation deployed in a single launch -- for instance: - We can do distributed optics, with each satellite hosting a camera, allowing us to do extremely fast revisits, image stacking, 3d stereo optics, etc. While each individual camera is worse than a larger, more traditional camera, by leveraging 20-100 of them, it starts to outperform individual earth observation satellites. - Deployable mesh networks: a large / government-owned and operated satellite could host a cannister of these satellites, ready to go, in the event of adversarial attack or disrupted radio communications -- and rapidly deploy a mesh radio network on-demand. Think of it as a cell network on demand. - Aggregate data collection: dispense a constellation into a space weather storm, patch of high-density neutral particles, etc. to capture data with extreme accuracy. We've licensed tech from a university that can measure both space weather and neutral particle density to sub-meter resolution, allowing us to generate extremely accurate ionosphere maps, for instance. This single-board platform lets us test experimental tech, validate it, license it for market, etc. very rapidly. - Batch testing in space: the bread-and-butter of the company is rapid prototyping and batch testing in space. We can host a component to test, deploy them in-situ across 100 satellites at a lower price point than on-ground testing, and generate 100 hours of space qualification time per real-world hour. You could get 73,000 hours of space qual time in one month, for cheaper than on-ground testing, with a faster turnaround time as these things are mass produced, ready to go. ** We are currently closing our Pre-Seed round, and will update the funding amount section when the deal goes through. This Pre-Seed round will allow us to meet certain technical and market entry milestones to begin leveraging our $5M Seed Round.

companies.name: WellCapped
companies.description: WellCapped enables members to access a shared inventory of high quality wigs and hair extensions. Members are able to access this inventory through three ways: monthly subscription, a-la-carte rentals, and purchasing through our resale program. On average, a wig made with human hair costs $600. This is not including the additional money that consumers spend to have the wig installed. Consumers in the United States are currently spending $1800 annually on human hair extensions and wigs. Our members save money and have more versatility by paying a monthly fee to have a wig shipped to them each month. The wigs are also specially made so that they are easily self-installed by our members, from the comfort of their homes, saving them time and money. We use local contractors to handle the sanitization and restyling of the wigs once the wig is returned. In the future, we want to add an AR component that allows members to virtually try on wigs using an app. Additionally, we use predictive modeling to recommend styles and will eventually scale this model out to products in adjacent categories such as shampoo and conditioner. We are starting with wigs because consumers who wear wigs are typically hyper-consumers of beauty products. This allows us to collect enough data to place our members in hives, which are groups of members with similar preferences. We will use k-means clustering to build the model that will recommend products to our members based on their hive and historical rentals/purchases.

companies.name: KovaDx
companies.description: As KovaDx, our mission is to bridge the gaps in care by developing monitoring tools for rare blood diseases, starting with Sickle Cell Disease (SCD). Due to historical underinvestment, there is a lack of drugs and interventions available to support disease management. Insufficient research funding has resulted in a limited understanding of the disease mechanisms and minimal advancements in the standard of care. Unfortunately, other rare red blood diseases face similar challenges, with inadequate investment and a lack of tools for drug discovery, development, and care management. To address these issues, we are creating a revolutionary diagnostic and monitoring device that combines Quantitative Phase Imaging, Machine Learning, and Microfluidics. This device allows us to analyze red blood cells, examining various parameters such as CBC parameters and the flexibility of the cell membrane. This technology has tremendous potential for translational research in drug discovery and development, enhancing the therapeutic pipeline for rare blood diseases. In the clinical setting, our tool will support care management by monitoring blood health. It will enable a better understanding of the effects of different interventions and aid in predicting and preventing the worst outcomes.

companies.name: Ag-Defense Systems
companies.description: Ag-Defense Systems, Inc. (ADS) is a food safety technology company dedicated to moving food safety from a reactive approach based on food recalls to a preventative approach based on testing and culling contaminated food prior to market delivery. ADS will achieve this goal by delivering user-friendly foodborne pathogen testing technology to food processing companies so that testing can be done in-house rather than at third-party testing laboratories. This technology will be designed so that non-scientific staff within food processing plants can perform foodborne pathogen testing, thus eliminating the time delays associated with third-party testing. Our nation's current food safety approach relies on the consumer to be the "sensor" of contaminated food in the market which usually results in a food recall, whereby millions of pounds of product is removed from the market at the food processor's expense. In contrast, direct testing by food processors with ADS' technology will allow contaminated food to be culled prior to market delivery, thereby saving processors millions in expenses and enhancing public health.\.

Today’s road inspections are either expensive and highly accurate—like laser vans costing over a million dollars—or cheap and extremely unreliable, such as smartphone-based apps. This leaves only well-funded cities with access to quality data, while smaller municipalities are forced to make critical maintenance decisions based on outdated or inaccurate information. To bridge this gap, PaveX offers a low-cost, high-accuracy solution designed for cities of all sizes. Our compact, vehicle-mounted system—priced under $2,500—uses depth-enabled cameras and AI to generate industry-standard road condition ratings. This is especially urgent in the Midwest and Northeast, where harsh winters cause road damage to appear quickly and unpredictably. With inspections typically done every one to three years, cities are left blind to emerging issues. PaveX enables frequent, scalable assessments—giving municipalities the real-time data they need to maintain safer, longer-lasting roads while saving billions in long-term repair costs.

companies.description: What RHVR Does - In Simple Terms: RHVR created a breakthrough visual tool designed for this new era of AI and Large Language Models (LLMs). It makes fixing computer code in any programming language much easier, safer, and faster while helping both AI and humans better understand code patterns and structures. The Problem: Big companies have millions of lines of old software code that's hard to understand and risky to change. companies.name: Basin Technologies
companies.description: Wind-blown dust is a costly, everyday problem. When land is disturbed by construction, mining, farming, military training ranges, or solar development, dry soil lifts into the air. That dust hurts air quality and public health, cuts visibility on highways, fouls equipment, and lowers the output of solar panels. The usual fixes, such as spraying water, spreading chemical suppressants, or laying gravel, are expensive, need constant reapplication, use a lot of water, or create their own environmental problems. This technology takes a different approach: engineered roughness arrays. These are carefully patterned arrangements of surface elements placed on the ground. By tuning their shape, height, and spacing, the array changes how wind flows right at the surface, slowing it down where it would otherwise pick up loose soil. The result is less dust lifted into the air, with far less water and chemical use than conventional methods. The science behind it comes from research at the Desert Research Institute, part of the Nevada System of Higher Education, building on decades of work studying how wind moves sediment across arid landscapes. Our team is exploring whether this research can solve real problems for the people who deal with dust every day: land managers, contractors, mine operators, defense agencies, and energy developers. We are at the earliest stage of that exploration. The purpose of this work is to talk to potential users, understand where dust control costs them the most, and learn whether an engineered-roughness solution would fit how they actually operate. companies.name: Perceptive Robotics
companies.description: Perceptive Robotics is building the sensing layer for endovascular intervention. In a stroke thrombectomy, fluoroscopy shows where the catheter is, not what its tip is touching: clot, vessel wall, or open lumen. That distinction decides whether the next aspiration attempt works, and today it is inferred rather than observed. One in three thrombectomies still misses on the first pass. LumenSense is a small module that clips onto the hub of the aspiration catheter a hospital already buys, reads a pressure signature from outside the body, and tells the operator what the tip is against before suction starts, like a parking sensor. Nothing else changes: no new catheter, console, capital equipment, workflow, or billing code. Because it never touches the patient, it also skips the biocompatibility and sterilization work that sets most device schedules. Eight years of Vanderbilt research, validated in four in-vivo porcine studies.

companies.name: RELIXA SYSTEMS INC
companies.description: Relixa Systems Inc is an applied-AI company solving a problem that has become foundational in the era of enterprise AI entity matching. Businesses hold the same customer, product, or supplier under different names, formats, and IDs across dozens of databases and every AI system built on top of that data inherits the confusion. When an LLM retrieves three conflicting records for the same customer, it doesn't resolve the conflict, it hallucinates around it. Clean, deduplicated, entity-resolved data is the unglamorous prerequisite for trustworthy enterprise AI. Relixa trains and deploys machine learning models that learn what "the same entity" looks like in a customer's data, then match at scale. Our technology builds on more than a decade of data-integration and ML research at UW–Madison, where our co-founder and Chief Scientist AnHai Doan led the research group behind widely used open-source entity-matching tools (Magellan, Sparkly, Delex, MatchFlow). companies.name: LubaLabs

By providing early insights into tissue stiffening, a key driver of fibrosis, LubaLabs helps improve disease detection and enables more reliable evaluation of potential anti-fibrotic drugs.

companies.name: Vialign

Vialign offers precise, robust and easy-to-install displacement sensing, integrated on a photonic chip.

The team identified that incremental improvements were not enough—fundamental innovation was needed to unlock real industrial impact. By focusing on next-generation system architectures, FlowVolta is building electrochemical systems for hydrogen production that deliver higher performance while remaining economically viable at scale. Their approach combines engineering innovation with a strong understanding of industrial requirements, ensuring that solutions are not only technically advanced but also practical to implement. These advancements are particularly important as hydrogen becomes a key pillar in decarbonizing sectors such as heavy industry, mobility, and energy storage. Improving the efficiency and scalability of electrochemical systems directly reduces the cost of hydrogen, accelerating its adoption worldwide. FlowVolta’s mission is to enable a new generation of electrochemical production technologies that support a cleaner, more sustainable energy system. The result is a hybrid binder that can be used in existing asphalt plants and helps reduce CO₂ emissions in road infrastructure while maintaining performance standards. By embedding ultrasound sensors in the tip of the ablation catheter, Sonic Precision provides imaging and sensing capabilities during the intervention, allowing the electrophysiologist to adapt the procedure to patient-specific characteristics. With this closed-loop approach, the venture aspires to create a new standard in the treatment of rhythm disorders in the heart by offering better options for the individual patient.

companies.name: VitalWear

companies.funding_notes: Verified domain pravah.com (Pravāh); Stanford-founded AI/foundation-model and physics-based grid intelligence startup for utilities and power systems, co-founders Mohak Mangal (CEO), Dhruv Suri (CTO) and Aman Gupta; PearX S25; works with utilities in the US, Germany and India. The company site names Vinod Khosla (Khosla Ventures), Sara Guo (Conviction) and Mar Hershenson (Pear VC) as backers, and Times of India (Nov 2025) confirms Khosla, Pear and Conviction backing. Funding amount (~$7M, or $7.5M in a later job listing) appears only on the company's own social profile and a Built In job post, with no round type, date or press release, so it is left out of rounds and total. Treated as unclear-round-type.

companies.name: Prohost AI
companies.description: AI property manager for short-term rental hosts
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain prohost.ai (ProhostAI); New York City-based AI property manager / 'AI employees' platform for short-term rental hosts; co-founders Bill Ulammandakh (CEO, ex-Airbnb) and Andrew Lawson (CTO, ex-Dropbox); YC Summer 2024. The company's About page says it has raised $2.6M from investors including Y Combinator and Pear VC, cumulative and with no round breakdown, dates or leads. Trackers mention a ~$1.5M 2024 'seed', but no press release or news confirms a priced seed, so round type is unclear (likely YC/accelerator plus SAFE-style early money).

companies.name: Quadric.io
companies.description: Semiconductor IP for on-device AI inference
companies.funding_notes: Input domain quadric.io is the legacy domain; the company now uses quadric.ai (same Quadric, Inc., Burlingame, CA; CEO Veerbhan Kheterpal, co-founders from 21 Inc./Earn.com). Licenses programmable GPNPU (Chimera) AI-inference processor IP. Seed led by Pear (amount undisclosed), $15M Series A led by DENSO/NSITEXE (May 2019), $21M Series B led by NSITEXE (Mar 2022), $30M Series C first close led by ACCELERATE Fund/BEENEXT (Jan 2026; total then $72M), and a $16M second close led by IFC (Jul 2026), bringing the Series C to $46M and total raised to $90M per the company.

companies.name: Quansa
companies.description: Employee financial wellness platform with earned wage access
companies.funding_notes: Domain quansa.io not fetched directly, but company name, description and Pear accelerator link match. Quansa is a Chile/Brazil employer-sponsored financial-wellness and earned-wage-access fintech founded 2020 by Mafalda Barros and Gonzalo Blanco (Stanford Startup Garage, Pear accelerator). $3.6M seed led by Valor Capital Group with Pear VC, Canary, Norte, Magma, Sequoia Scouts and angels (press release via LAVCA, Jul 2021; LatamList, Exame). No later rounds found.

companies.name: Radar Therapeutics
companies.description: RNA-sensing mRNA therapeutics that target specific cell types
companies.funding_notes: Input website rnasensing.bio is the Stanford academic RADAR (RNA sensing using ADAR) resource site from the co-founders' lab, not the company's site; the company's domain is radartx.bio. Radar Therapeutics, Berkeley, CA; CEO Sophia Lugo, CSO Eerik Kaseniit, co-founders Xiaojing Gao (Stanford) and Jim Collins (MIT). Oversubscribed $13.4M seed led by NfX Bio with Eli Lilly, Biovision, KdT, Pear VC, BEVC and others (BusinessWire, May 23, 2024). No later rounds found.

companies.name: Range Biotechnologies
companies.description: End-to-end platform for translational proteomics
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain range.bio; San Francisco-based translational proteomics company (high-throughput multiplexed protein quantification) founded by Stanford labmates Brandon Wilson (CEO) and Nicolo Maganzini (CTO) with Prof. Tom Soh. $5.2M seed led by ARTIS Ventures with Pear VC, Page One, Civilization Ventures, Pillar, Four Cities Capital, Hawktail and others (GlobeNewswire, Jun 12, 2023). No later rounds found.

companies.name: Real Sports
companies.description: Social app for live sports data and fan discussion
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain: realapp.link redirects to realapp.com (Real Sports App); legal entity Real Vault, Inc. (SEC address Westmont, IL, Chicago area). Social live box-score/play-by-play app founded 2020 (beta)/2021 by brothers John and Louis Antonelli; ~700K-900K DAU per Front Office Sports. FOS (Apr 13, 2026) reports The Chernin Group led a minority-stake round with past/present investors Pear, Tamarisk Lane, Operator Partners and NBA players; amount and valuation undisclosed. SEC Form D (filed 2026-04-21) shows $12,090,494 equity sold, first sale 2026-02-27, 25 investors, matching that round. Round type not stated in any allowed source: trackers conflict (Caplight/input say Series A, Tracxn says Series B) and the 'Series A' label appears only on LinkedIn, so marked unclear-round-type. Earlier rounds (a reported 2022 seed with Pear) have no public amount.

companies.name: Reduct.video
companies.description: Transcript-based platform for searching and editing video
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain reduct.video; San Francisco-based transcript-based video search/editing platform (CEO Prabhas Pokharel, CTO Robert Ochshorn); customers have included Intuit, Autodesk, Facebook, Spotify. $4M round led by Greylock and South Park Commons, with angels Dylan Field, Armando Mann and Elad Gil (TechCrunch and company blog, Feb 11, 2021). Greylock's investment post says it 'signed up to lead the seed', and its portfolio page lists first partnered at Seed. No later rounds found. Pear's check is not broken out.

companies.name: Rely Health
companies.description: Hybrid human-AI care navigation for health systems
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain relyhealth.care (www redirects); AI-plus-human care navigation / patient orchestration ('AI front desk with a human in the loop') for health systems. Formed in Feb 2023 when Healthful, a startup incubated by Inflect Health (Vituity's innovation hub), merged with Sympto and expanded as Rely Health; Inflect's post (seen only in search snippets, page blocked) notes Pear VC's Mar Hershenson took part. Backed by Inflect Health and Pear, but no amount, date or round type is disclosed in any allowed source. Pear's portfolio lists Series A, and a Caplight figure (~$2.08M) doesn't clearly match this company; neither was used. Caveat: an unrelated 'Rely' (real-estate diligence, $4.5M seed led by 2048 Ventures) shows up in searches and is not this company.

companies.name: Remuner
companies.description: AI platform automating sales commissions and incentive management
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain remuner.com; Barcelona, Spain-based AI sales-compensation/commission platform founded 2023 (CEO Sergio González). Pre-seed of €2M led by Pear VC (Jan 2024; K Fund, Bonsai Partners, Enzo Ventures, Wayra, BStartup and angels). €5.5M (~$6.5M) seed led by Seaya with significant Pear VC participation (Sept 2025, EU-Startups/Tech.eu/company blog); Beatriz González (Seaya) and Pepe Agell (Pear) joined the board. Total about €7.5M.

companies.name: rePurpose
companies.description: Packaging sustainability and EPR compliance platform for brands
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain repurpose.global; rePurpose Global, Inc. (Delaware; SEC address Miami, FL; offices in New York and Bangalore), packaging sustainability, plastic-recovery credit and EPR compliance platform founded 2017 by Svanika Balasubramanian (CEO), Peter Wang-Hjemdahl and Aditya Siroya. SEC Form D filed 2023-05-04 shows $19,983,428 equity sold (12 investors). Penny Jar Capital (Stephen Curry) announced its investment June 2023, and Unreasonable Group lists backers Left Lane Capital, Emerson Collective, Penny Jar and Pear VC. The 2023 round is widely called a Series A, but that label comes only from trackers and a co-founder's LinkedIn post, not an allowed source, so it's marked unclear-round-type. Lead not confirmed from a primary source. Earlier: a Pear investment (~$150K, Apr 2020, per a LinkedIn post) and a 2021 seed (tracker-only), neither used.

companies.name: ResiQuant
companies.description: AI underwriting platform for catastrophe-exposed property insurers
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain resiquant.ai; San Francisco-based AI underwriting/property-intelligence platform for catastrophe-exposed (seismic, wind, wildfire) property insurers, founded by Stanford Blume Center structural-engineering PhDs Omar Issa (CEO) and Francisco Galvis; PearX S24. $4M seed led by LDV Capital with Foothill Ventures, Pear VC, Alumni Ventures and angels (company release Mar 14, 2025; The Insurer). SEC Form D (filed Jan 2025) shows $4,649,996 equity sold, first sale 2024-12-23, 8 investors; it likely includes the seed plus earlier money, so amount_raised uses the announced $4M. No Series A found.

companies.name: Rollout
companies.description: Embedded integrations platform for SaaS products
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain rollouthq.com (now branded at rollout.com); co-founder AK Lalani; reportedly Austin, TX. Started as an embedded Zapier-style integrations platform for SaaS (matches the input), rebuilt as Rollout V2 in 2023, and now sells a 'Universal API' for real estate and mortgage CRMs, transaction management and LOS systems. Pear lists it as a portfolio company (Seed), but no press release, news report or SEC Form D with a funding amount or round was found. Trackers cite a ~$3.81M seed in Jan 2020 (Base10, Musha Ventures, Pear, Reform Ventures), but that relies only on PitchBook-type data and isn't used here.

companies.name: SalesPatriot
companies.description: AI operating system for defense and aerospace procurement
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain salespatriot.com; Polish-American (US plus Warsaw R&D centre) AI procurement platform for defense and aerospace parts distributors and manufacturers, founded 2024 by Nelson Ray (CEO), Benjamin Rhodes-Kropf (CTO) and Maciej Szymczyk; YC-backed. $5M seed led by CRV with Pear VC, Y Combinator, SV Angel, Liquid2, Uncorrelated Ventures and angels (Tech.eu/EU-Startups, Oct 28, 2025), bringing total funding to $6.3M. The ~$1.3M earlier pre-seed/YC money is not broken out. No Series A found.

companies.name: Savvi AI
companies.description: AI platform for banks and fintechs to build and own AI apps
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain savviai.com; SAVVI AI Inc. (SEC address Kentfield, CA), platform letting banks, credit unions and fintechs build and own governed AI apps/agents (founded 2020). SEC Form D filings show a 2021 convertible-note offering ($1,325,000 sold, first sale 2021-01-29, 11 investors; excluded from the equity total) and a 2023 equity offering ($5,468,184 sold of $7,137,680 offered, first sale 2023-09-01, 36 investors). Chicago Ventures lists it as a 2023 portfolio company. No press release or reputable news names the round type or lead: trackers variously call it seed or Series A (input says Series A), so it's marked unclear-round-type.

companies.name: SellScale
companies.description: AI agent that automates outbound sales pipeline building
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain sellscale.com; San Francisco AI outbound-sales/SDR automation company founded by Ishan Sharma (CEO) and Aakash Adesara (ex-Athelas; DailyDropout.FYI). The company blog (Nov 17, 2022) announces a $3.4M 'inception round' led by Pear VC (Pejman Nozad), and TechCrunch (Dec 6, 2022) reports it as $3M led by Pear with Ovo Fund and Browder Capital. Pear's portfolio shows it entered at Pre-Seed, and the round isn't called a seed in any primary source, so it's treated as pre-seed. No later priced seed or Series A found (Pear lists the current stage as Seed; trackers call the round seed). Caveat: it could be argued as unclear-round-type.

companies.name: Senti Bio
companies.description: Gene circuit-powered cell therapies for incurable cancers

funding_rounds.stage: IPO (SPAC merger with Dynamics Special Purpose Corp.)

grants.name: California Institute for Regenerative Medicine (CIRM) grant

companies.funding_notes: Verified domain sentibio.com; Senti Biosciences, South San Francisco gene-circuit CAR-NK cell therapy company (CEO Tim Lu; co-founders Jim Collins, Wilson Wong, Philip Lee), Nasdaq: SNTI. $53M Series A led by NEA with Pear Ventures participating (Feb 2018), and $105M Series B led by Leaps by Bayer (Jan 2021), for ~$158M private total (amount_raised = pre-IPO private equity). Went public via SPAC merger with Dynamics Special Purpose Corp. in June 2022 (~$140.3M gross incl. $50.6M PIPE). Post-IPO PIPE led by Celadon Partners: $37.6M (Dec 2024) plus ~$10M (Jan 2025) = $47.6M. $8M CIRM grant ($6.4M received by Jan 2025). 2026: up to $40M of senior secured convertible notes to a Celadon affiliate (Apr 2026; $16M issued by Sept), Nasdaq bid-price/equity deficiency notices (Aug 2026), and on Oct 15, 2026 stockholders approved a merger with Celadon-controlled ST NewCo plus CVRs worth up to $60M tied to SENTI-202 milestones. Pear's input entry stage 'Seed' predates the Series A.

companies.name: Sequel
companies.description: Redesigned tampon engineered for comfort and reliability
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain trysequel.com; Sequel (US, remote team of about 7) makes a patented spiral-design tampon, FDA-cleared 2023; founded 2018 by Stanford engineers and athletes Greta Meyer and Amanda Calabrese. Launched Dec 21, 2021 with a $5M seed (BusinessWire/Femtech Insider) from MaC VC, Pear Accelerator, Long Journey, Ulu, Graph Ventures and angels. Forbes calls it combined pre-seed and seed money, with MaC VC as lead. Sportico (Mar 2026) says Sequel has raised over $8M (per Forbes, June 2025), with investors including RRE Ventures, and that Tipt Ventures invested in late 2025 (amount undisclosed); an official Series A is planned. amount_raised = the 'over $8M' reported total, so treat it as a lower bound.

companies.name: Series
companies.description: AI-powered social network connecting users via iMessage
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain series.so; AI social network that works through iMessage, making double opt-in introductions. Founded 2025 by Yale students Nathaneo Johnson (CEO) and Sean Hargrow; office in Chelsea, New York. $3.1M pre-seed led by Parable (Anne Lee Skates) with Pear VC, DGB.VC and others (GlobeNewswire, Apr 2025). TechCrunch (Apr 24, 2026) reports a $5.1M pre-seed. The $5.1M likely includes the earlier $3.1M (not stated), so amount_raised = $5.1M, not $8.2M. A Business Insider URL slug mentions 'seed', but every primary report calls it pre-seed.

companies.name: Seven Starling
companies.description: Virtual mental health care for mothers and women
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain sevenstarling.com; Washington, DC-based (launched from New York) virtual women's/perinatal mental health provider, founded by HBS grads Tina Beilinson Keshani (CEO) and Sophia Richter; PearX S20. $2.9M seed co-led by Pear VC, Expa and Magnify Ventures (Sept 2021); $10.9M Series A led by RH Capital (July 2024); $8M Series A-Prime led by Rethink Impact (Sept 2025, per the press release and Mintz). Total about $21.8M. Operates in 18 states and targets 30+ by end of 2026.

companies.name: Smarty.AI
companies.description: AI assistant for scheduling, tasks, and workflow automation
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain smarty.ai; founded 2018 by solo founder Denzil Eden (MIT CS/AI, Harvard MBA, ex-Microsoft) as an AI executive assistant for scheduling and tasks (matches the input). The site now markets a 'Chief of AI' subscription (embedded AI engineering team building automations and agents for businesses), so the company appears to have pivoted toward AI services. Starter Story's founder profile (Oct 2024) says Smarty raised $2.5M, without round types, dates or investors. Trackers list a ~$600K Jan 2020 round (Pear, Sterling Road, Motivate Ventures and others) and an undisclosed Nov 2021 seed (Amplify.LA, Pear), but these are tracker-only and not used. No press release or Form D found. Caveat: the $2.5M rests on a founder-interview site, not a listed news outlet.

companies.name: Sniffspot
companies.description: Marketplace to rent private land as dog parks
companies.funding_notes: Verified domain sniffspot.com; Seattle-founded (2018, CEO David Adams) marketplace for renting private yards and land as dog parks, which moved to a membership model in late 2024. Inc. (July 3, 2026) reports $4.4M raised to date, no new capital since 2020, revenue up from $3M (2024) to $6M (2025), ~40 staff, and cash-flow positive. No allowed source gives round types, dates or leads. Trackers describe a ~$4.5M seed with Pear VC, Unpopular Ventures and Leap Venture Studio (latest Oct 2020), but that isn't used, so it's marked unclear-round-type. Pear entered at Pre-Seed.

companies.name: SnoutID
companies.description: Payment and financing platform for veterinary practices
companies.funding_notes: SnoutID now operates as Snout (snoutid.com redirects to snout.com); pet wellness-plan financing platform for veterinary clinics, founded 2023 by Emily Dong per Fortune, offices in Michigan/San Francisco/New York. On 2026-01-28 announced a $10M Series A led by Footwork with existing investors Pear, Bread and Butter Ventures, Restive Ventures (Footwork's post also names Griffon Partners), plus a separate $100M debt/financing facility from Clear Haven Capital Management (debt, excluded from equity total). Earlier pre-seed/seed amounts not publicly disclosed, so $10M is only the disclosed equity.

companies.name: Socratix AI
companies.description: AI agents for fraud and risk team investigations
companies.funding_notes: Verified getsocratix.ai. Bay Area/San Francisco company (founded 2025 by Riya Jagetia and Satya Vasanth Tumati, YC-backed) building AI coworkers for fraud and risk investigations. Announced a $4.1M seed round on 2025-10-28 led by Pear VC with Y Combinator, Twenty Two Ventures, Transpose Platform Management and angels. No later rounds found.

companies.name: Solvvy
companies.description: AI-powered conversational automation platform
companies.funding_notes: Solvvy (solvvy.com, now offline after acquisition), Palo Alto, CA conversational AI/self-service customer support platform led by founding CEO Mahesh Ram. Raised a $12M Series A on 2017-10-23 led by Scale Venture Partners with existing investors Pear Ventures, Signatures Capital and True Ventures, bringing total funding to $16.5M (the ~$4.5M of earlier funding is not itemized publicly). Zoom announced the acquisition on 2022-05-12 and closed it 2022-05-19 for $121.2M cash per Zoom's SEC filing.

companies.name: Spur
companies.description: Agentic QA platform for e-commerce sites
companies.funding_notes: Verified spurtest.com. New York City-based agentic QA company (YC, founded 2024 by Yale grads Sneha Sivakumar and Anushka Nijhawan) using AI browser agents to test e-commerce/consumer sites. Raised $4.5M seed announced 2025-04-17, led by First Round Capital (Liz Wessel) with Pear VC, Neo, Conviction, Liquid2Ventures, Predictive Venture Partners and angels. No later rounds found.

companies.name: Stan
companies.description: All-in-one e-commerce platform for content creators
companies.funding_notes: Verified stan.store. Creator storefront/monetization platform founded 2020 by John Hu and Vitalii Dodonov (Los Angeles area). Its only priced round is a $5M seed led by Forerunner Ventures (announced around Jan/Feb 2022; some sources say 2021) with Pear VC and angels Kevin Hartz and Michael Ovitz; Forbes (Aug 2025) says it has been profitable since and hasn't needed more capital. In 2025 Steven Bartlett (May) and Gary Vaynerchuk (Sept) invested on undisclosed terms (per Contrary Research), not counted in the total.

companies.name: Stellation
companies.description: AI-powered provider analytics and insights
companies.funding_notes: Verified stellationcare.com (Stellation Care), AI provider analytics / provider intelligence and referral optimization for health plans and risk-bearing provider groups, led by Michelle Xie (CEO) and Kathy Qian. Acquired by Skylight Health (Nashville) on 2026-01-07, terms not disclosed. Pear lists it as a Pre-Seed investment; aggregator sites list COREangels, Leadout Capital, MedMountain Ventures, Foundry and Pear as investors and mention a seed, but no public sourced round announcement, amount or date was found (tracker-only), so classified as pre-seed/angel only.

companies.name: Sudozi
companies.description: AI-powered procurement and vendor management platform
companies.funding_notes: Verified sudozi.com. Austin, TX finance/procurement and vendor-management software founded by Rose Punkunus (former CFO of Uber U.S. & Canada). Closed a $4.3M seed round announced 2022-05-12, led by Pear VC with S3 Ventures, Mischief and 40+ angels. Acquired by Zone & Co (announced 2026-04-09), terms not disclosed.

companies.name: SweatPals
companies.description: Community-driven fitness platform building connections through movement
companies.funding_notes: Verified sweatpals.com. Austin, TX community fitness marketplace for in-person workouts/events, co-founded by Salar Shahini (CEO) and Mandi Zhou. Raised $12M seed announced 2025-10-28, led by Patron, a16z speedrun and Kevin Hart's HartBeat Ventures, with WndrCo, Antler, Pear, Max Mullen and Deb Liu; company says this brings total funding to $17.2M. The earlier ~$5.2M (pre-seed/earlier rounds) is not itemized publicly.

companies.name: Switchmate
companies.description: The snap-on smart light switch
companies.funding_notes: Switchmate Inc. (Pleasanton, CA; Robert Romano exec/director), maker of a snap-on smart light switch; it rebranded as Simply Smart Home (input site mysimplysmarthome.com, whose About page says the company was originally Switchmate). The only public funding record is an SEC Form D for $350,000 equity, first sale 2014-10-14 (round type not stated; Pear lists it as a Pre-Seed investment; trackers also name Highway1 and Dunelm Energy). No priced seed or later round found. Pear's portfolio marks it Acquired, but no acquisition announcement was found; it appears to be a rebrand, not an acquisition.

companies.name: TeachFX
companies.description: AI-powered instructional feedback for teachers
companies.funding_notes: Verified teachfx.com. Bay Area (Stanford-origin) AI instructional feedback app for teachers, founded by Jamie Poskin (CEO) and Berk Coker. $10M Series A announced 2022-09-29, led by Reach Capital with Osage Venture Partners, Pearson Ventures, Brighteye Ventures, Ulu Ventures and Newfund. The founder letter confirms an earlier seed round (Reach, Brighteye, Ulu, Newfund); Reach says it first invested in 2017. Seed amounts are only on trackers (Dealroom: ~$350K Jun 2017 with Pear/Reach and ~$1.1M Nov 2017), not confirmed by primary sources, so the equity total counts only the $10M Series A.

companies.name: TeachShare
companies.description: AI platform for differentiated curriculum development
companies.funding_notes: Verified teachshare.com. AI platform for teachers to plan, differentiate and assess curriculum, launched January 2024 by UC Berkeley dropouts Aryan Bhadouria (CEO) and Adam Goldstein (CTO); Forbes 30 Under 30 Education 2026. Forbes says the founders have raised $2.3M from groups including Reach Capital; Pear backed it at pre-seed per Pear's portfolio. No public announcement naming a priced seed round (only trackers call it seed), so round type is unclear. Cumulative total, possibly multiple rounds.

companies.name: Topsort
companies.description: AI monetization infrastructure for retailers and marketplaces
companies.funding_notes: Verified topsort.com. San Francisco retail media / auction-based ad infrastructure for retailers and marketplaces, founded 2021 by Regina Ye (CEO), Francisco Larrain and Stanford GSB professor Michael Ostrovsky. Seed announced 2022-03-10 at a $110M valuation (TechCrunch/FinSMEs report $8M; the company's 2024 release says $8.6M, which is used here). $20M Series A announced 2024-03-04 led by Upload Ventures with returning Quiet Capital and Pear Ventures, at a $150M valuation. Total equity is about $28.6M ($28M if the seed was $8M). Trackers mention a 2021 pre-seed; not counted.

companies.name: TownHound
companies.description: Real-time, utilization based mobile offers for local restaurants
companies.funding_notes: TownHound was a San Francisco app offering real-time, off-peak mobile deals for local restaurants, co-founded around 2015 by Bryan Solar and Alex Russell. Founder bios report it was acquired by Google in 2016, about eight months after launch; terms not disclosed. The input website (ads.google.com) is the acquirer's product, not TownHound's own domain, which appears defunct. Pear lists it as a Pre-Seed investment; no public round amount or priced round was found.

companies.name: Transcera
companies.description: Ceramide-based oral delivery platform for biologic drugs

grants.name: NIH/NIDDK SBIR Phase I (1R43DK134260-01A1): oral GLP-1 ceramide conjugates

companies.funding_notes: Transcera Inc. (Cambridge, MA; SBIR contacts use @transcera.bio emails; transcera.bio now redirects to transcera.com) is building a ceramide/glycosphingolipid platform for oral delivery of biologics such as GLP-1, based on Harvard professor Wayne Lencer's research; CEO Hunter Goble, CSO Justin Wolfe; PearX S21. Announced a seed round in July 2023 led by Xora Innovation (Temasek), with Tau Ventures and existing pre-seed investors Pear, Digitalis Ventures and KdT Ventures; amount not disclosed. Also won an NIH SBIR Phase I grant of $324,905 (2023), listed only under grants.

companies.name: Trimz
companies.description: AI platform for creating, sharing, and watching animated short videos
companies.funding_notes: Trimz (trimz.ai now redirects to trimz.tv), San Francisco app for creating and watching AI-generated animated/anime short series, founded by Nicholas Pezzotti and Nikhil Gopalam. Pear lists a Pre-Seed investment. Only trackers (Caplight/PitchBook-class) mention a round around July 2025, with no amount; no press release or news coverage found.

companies.name: True & Co
companies.description: Online bra fitting service and shop
companies.funding_notes: Verified trueandco.com (True&Co), San Francisco online bra-fit quiz and lingerie retailer founded 2012 by Michelle Lam. $2M seed in May 2012 (First Round, SoftTech VC, SoftBank Capital, Aileen Lee) and $4M more in Oct 2013 (Crosslink, VegasTechFund, Pejman Nozad, FundersClub plus existing investors). TechCrunch doesn't name the 2013 round; trackers call it Series A. Disclosed rounds total $6M, but TechCrunch (2017) says it raised a reported $13M in total, so later rounds went undisclosed. PVH (Calvin Klein's owner) acquired it in March 2017 for an undisclosed price, reportedly in the tens of millions, with investors mostly getting their money back.

companies.name: TrueMeter
companies.description: AI utility management for multi-location businesses
companies.funding_notes: Verified truemeter.com (formerly EcoTrove; PearX W25), AI utility-bill management and energy savings for multi-location brick-and-mortar businesses, co-founded by Ozge Islegen-Wojdyla and Ali Sarilgan (Stanford). $4M seed announced 2025-09-10, led by Ulu Ventures with Pear VC, e2.vc, RiverPark, Flex Capital, Sarah Smith Fund, Cyan, Costanoa and Sand Hill Angels. Company and Pear say total funding is now more than $5.5M; the earlier ~$1.5M (pre-seed) isn't itemized, and $5.5M is a floor.

companies.name: TruTec
companies.description: AI takeoffs for paving contractors from aerial imagery
companies.funding_notes: Verified trutec.ai (TruTec.ai, Inc., formerly Skyvo.ai, Inc.; Delaware), AI paving/landscaping/roofing takeoffs from aerial imagery plus estimating/CRM software; executives Ross Stitts (CEO) and Ryan Brown. SEC Form D filed 2026-07-09 (Rule 506(b)) reports $4,609,993 equity sold to 8 investors, first sale 2026-05-29, including $500,000 of cancelled (converted) convertible debt. The filing doesn't name the round; tracker sites and a founder social post (excluded) call it a seed, and Pear lists it as Seed, but no press release or news coverage confirms a priced seed, so it's classified unclear-round-type. Investors not named in public sources beyond Pear's portfolio listing.

companies.name: TruthSystems
companies.description: Real-time AI governance agent for regulated industries
companies.funding_notes: Verified truthsystems.ai (Truth Systems), San Francisco AI governance/compliance company whose product Charter enforces firm policies and client guidelines on AI use in real time, mainly for AmLaw 200 law firms; co-founders Alex (Anh) Mac and Nam Nguyen, Stanford Law-linked. $4M seed announced 2025-10-28 led by Gradient Ventures with Lightspeed, F-Prime, Y Combinator, The LegalTech Fund, Pear VC, a16z Scout, Silver Circle, WndrCo and angels. No later rounds found.

companies.name: Neopausia
companies.description: En Neopausia estamos creando una super app para la menopausia que busca empoderar, educar y tratar a las mujeres durante toda su transición menopáusica. Ofrecemos terapia de reemplazo hormonal y no hormonal, prescrita por médicos, respaldada por la ciencia y enviada directamente a tu puerta. El 95% de las mujeres no reciben una terapia eficaz e integral durante su menopausia y son alrededor de 42 millones de mujeres pasando por esta etapa solamente en LATAM. Dado que la mujer en promedio pasa más de un tercio de su vida en la etapa de perimenopausia a postmenopausia, la brecha en la atención es alarmante. Del 100% de mujeres pasan por la menopausia, 80% de ellas experimentan síntomas molestos hasta graves como menstruaciones irregulares, bochornos, dolores musculares y articulares, insomnio, incontinencia, cambios de ánimo, subida de peso, problemas sexuales entre otros (son 34 síntomas en total). Y es más: La mujer no solo sufre de síntomas durante la transición, sino que conforme va pasando el tiempo, también puede afectar su salud a largo plazo con un aumentado riesgo de enfermedades cardiovasculares, Alzheimer/demencia y osteoporosis. Al no tratarse o no tratarse correctamente baja su calidad de vida, salud, longevidad y capacidad productiva. El tratamiento más eficaz y el único aprobado por FDA es el tratamiento hormonal que regula la baja hormonal que ocurre durante esta transición en la mujer. El uso consistente por varios años no solo reduce los síntomas en un 90%, sino también lleva a una reducción de riesgo de mortalidad cardiovascular del 48% y baja la mortalidad general en un 30%. Aunque en Chile 90% de la población podría tomarlo, solo 5% de mujeres usan terapia de reemplazo hormonal. En muchos países de LATAM este % es aún más bajo. ¿Por qué pasa esto? Falta de educación: Muchas mujeres desconocen y confunden los síntomas y sufren sin solución (ej: cambios de ánimo lo tratan con antidepresivos, dolores musculares con kinesiología). Tabúes: Hay muchos tabúes y vergüenza, síntomas y sufrimiento se normalizan. Segmento desatendido: Falta de especialistas y desinformación del personal médico sobre el tema (hubo un estudio, origen de varias ramas más, que decían que las hormonas daban cáncer). ¿Qué hace Neopausia? En Neopausia nuestra misión es eliminar los tabúes y la confusión sobre la menopausia y ayudar a las mujeres a obtener las soluciones que necesitan. Estamos creando una super app para la menopausia que busca empoderar, educar y tratar a las mujeres durante toda su transición. Ofrecemos terapia de reemplazo hormonal, prescrita por médicos, respaldada por la ciencia y enviada directamente a tu puerta. ¿Cómo lo hacemos? Lo que destaca a Neopausia es el acompañamiento transversal en todo el viaje de la mujer. Acompañamos a las mujeres vía Whatsapp para ayudarles a armar su hoja de ruta personal. Este acompañamiento para volverse escalable, requiere de habilitadores tecnológicos: automatización, personalización de mensajes, manejo de BBDD, integración de e-commerce y e-learning. El viaje de la mujer consiste en: Educación: Programas digitales educativas desarrollados con expertas de salud femenina (Más de 200 mujeres ya participaron en nuestro piloto “Menopausia sin Misterios” que creamos junto a 6 expertas de salud femenina) Atención: Hacemos el match entre mujeres y especialistas.Creamos una red de especialistas aprobados por Neopausia - con enfoque de género, conocimiento y experiencia en el tratamiento de menopausia y mirada integral. Tratamiento: Entregamos el tratamiento hormonal recetado por médicos a la puerta de casa de nuestras pacientes, mes a mes para asegurar su uso continuado (durante la semana pasada realizamos un piloto de este paso y ya pudimos vender más de 200.000 CLP en tratamiento hormonal en conjunto con nuestra farmacia partner que nos permite llegar a precios hasta un 40-50% más bajo que las grandes cadenas). Fuentes: Menopause—Biology, consequences, supportive care, and therapeutic options - Susan R.
